subject: hydra
pitch:
Category: Monster.
Subject: five-headed hydra.
Style: God of War.
reasoning:
I'm planning a compact but detailed hydra design — a large body with four legs, a tail, and five necks each ending in a jawed head with eyes, horns, and teeth, styled with gritty God of War-esque elements like scale textures, scars, runes, and Nordic carvings, aiming to keep the implementation manageable at a few hundred lines.

I'm working out the joint hierarchy and chains: a root hip joint connecting to a spine chain up to the chest, a tail chain trailing back and dipping to ground level, a thick body sweep with elliptical cross-sections, four limb chains for the legs with clawed feet parented to the spine or hips, and five neck chains branching from the upper chest toward individual heads.

For each head I'm planning a buildHead function handling the skull, snout, jaw, teeth, eyes, horns, nostrils, and frill, with the head joint oriented using a forward-and-downward direction vector derived from the neck's tangent so each head faces naturally.

Defining head-local coordinates...

Adding teeth rows along the jaw, then working on glowing eye spheres with a slit-pupil texture for an orange-yellow glow effect.

Sweeping horns back with bezier curves, then adding a crest of spikes along the top of the head and small nostril spheres at the snout tip. For character variation, I'll give one head a scar across the eye using a thin pale box for that war-torn look.

Now I'm scaling the heads differently so the center head is biggest and the outer ones taper down, with a helper function to scale local points. Then I'm positioning the neck bases at the chest and working out each neck's height and outward splay so the heads fan out realistically.

Each neck curves back then forward with a joint chain of five points, ending with the head angled slightly down and outward. I'm tapering the neck radius from thick at the base to thin near the head, and applying countershading paint along the underside to give it a believable belly tone.

For color, I'm going with a God of War palette: desaturated slate-greens and dark charcoal for the scales, bone-cream for the belly, and bronze/gold war-accent ribs with a touch of blood red, plus some armor remnants like broken chains and spear fragments scattered on the body.

Now I'm adding battle-worn details: a spear stuck in the back, chain loops around the central neck, rune-engraved bronze cuffs, bone spikes running along the spine, and glowing orange rune decals on the chest, along with scar textures. I'm sweeping spikes along the dorsal line so each one points outward along the body's normal direction, then building the paint function that layers scale patterns with countershading for the body texture.

Still writing hide paint...

Now I'm working out the leg structure, placing shoulder and foot joints for the front limbs and figuring out the bend direction so the elbows kick backward naturally.

For the hind legs I'm building a three-segment digitigrade chain, checking that the limb lengths reach from hip to foot, and naming each joint uniquely per side using an L/R suffix convention.

Writing foot shape and claws...

I'll skip the knee armor and bronze guard idea and go with simple elbow spikes instead, then move on to building the tail chain extending back from the hips.

Working out the tail path points and tapering radius function, making sure it narrows to a small tip while staying thin enough to avoid odd bulges, and adding bone-blade spikes and fin spines along it.

Now I'm figuring out how to join the tail and spine into one continuous body sweep from a shared hip joint, deciding whether to unify them into a single catmull path or just accept a small seam between two separate sweeps.

Still shaping spine radii...

Now I'm figuring out where the necks branch off the chest, clustering five neck bases near the top with slight overlap, and naming the neck joint chains for each segment.

I'm assigning side tags (R2, R1, C, L1, L2) across the five necks and building corresponding joint names for necks, heads, and jaws, using a five-point catmull path resampled per neck, then defining the head joints for each.

For the head joint, I'm attaching it as a child of the final neck joint, tilting its direction downward-forward with some outward splay based on side, while keeping right/up axes consistent in world space. For decoration, I'm planning a small bronze cuff ring made from a short cylinder placed and oriented along the neck's tangent at roughly 45% down its length.

Rather than adding a glow to the cuff texture, I'll reserve the glow effect for the chest rune circle instead, and make the cuff texture a simple grey-background design with dark rune glyphs that gets tinted bronze by the material color. The cylinder's radius will follow the neck's taper function plus a small offset, oriented along the tangent direction at that point.

For the chain, I'm thinking of linking torus-shaped segments along a path draped diagonally around the neck, positioning each link using the path's position and tangent so it drapes naturally like a spiral.

Simplifying to small box or torus links placed at each frame along the chain, alternating geometry orientation slightly so it reads visually as linked chain segments rather than a smooth tube.

Now I'm adding the embedded weapons: a broken spear shaft jutting from the back with a splintered tip and a red cloth wrap, plus a broken sword blade stuck into the flank for extra battle damage detail.

Now I'm figuring out the crossguard and hilt rods, then placing a glowing rune decal on the chest using a surface ray to find the front-facing point, making sure it clears the neck geometry.

For the rune texture itself, I'm sketching a Valknut-style interlocking triangle motif in orange with small tick marks. I'm also considering a faint ember glow inside the mouth via a thin red tongue part instead of a separate light source, and noting that one of the heads should have a blinded, pale eye to contrast with the others.

Now I'm working out the eye texture variants (fiery vs. milky-blind) and assigning the blind one to a specific head and side, then building out the skull and snout geometry using frustum boxes scaled to a shared size factor.

I'm positioning the jaw joint and lower jaw bone so the upper snout and lower jaw meet nearly flush, then applying a pose rotation to open the mouth slightly, with the central head opening wider than the others for variation.

Since anything built after the pose lands in the new orientation, I need to build all jaw children—including teeth—before applying the pose. I'm now generating the upper teeth as a row of spikes along the jaw, spacing them by index with slightly tapering width and depth as they go back.

Still writing teeth placement logic...

Then I'm sketching out the overall part inventory for the head: skull, snout, jaw, tongue, roughly a dozen upper and ten lower teeth, two eyes, horns, a crest, and nostrils.

I'm computing brow rod positions and eye socket placement based on the skull's interpolated width profile, setting detail to 0.6 for fewer spike sides to keep triangle count manageable across the ~330 total parts.

Still working out eye socket placement...

Checking the geometry, the disc edges poke slightly outside the sphere radius either way, so I'll just accept a stylized floating effect rather than a perfect fit. Actually maybe simpler to skip the sphere entirely and use a decal approach, embedding the eye as a flat disc directly into the skull surface instead.

Setting up decal placement on the skull with outward direction and position, sizing it as an elongated almond shape with a slit for the eye texture, plus a browridge piece positioned to cast shadow over it. Then I'm sketching the horn as a bezier sweep curving back, up, and outward from the skull base to a forward-swept tip.

Adding a second shorter spike horn on the jaw, then building the crest spines as a polygon outline running along the top of the skull with alternating triangular peaks.

Still placing head geometry...

Now I'm thinking through the neck cuffs and chains, deciding each neck gets a cuff plus possibly an iron collar, with extras for the outer neck. I'm also working out the neck coloring, using a front-facing normal check to apply striped belly-color plates, nesting paint functions so the result can return another paint call.

For the heads, I'm setting a mottled dark olive color scheme and letting the scale pattern reuse the same seed so it blends consistently with the neck. I'm deciding against extra flourishes like war paint or scars, and weighing adding small texture details like eye textures, a glowing rune circle on the chest, and a rune band on the cuffs, while considering whether a torn cloth or an axe stuck in one of the necks would fit a God of War aesthetic.

Lodging an axe in the right shoulder/chest area, defining its half-moon frosty blue blade with a faint rune glow, and working out the handle's rod coordinates and extrusion direction so it pierces convincingly into the body.

Working out the shaft and blade coordinates so the weapon's head sits near the top of the shaft, angled to one side and embedded into the chest.

Now I'm setting up the module imports from the builder library and sketching the metadata structure, then moving to the eye's SVG shape with an almond outline and a radial gradient fill.

Writing eye and blind SVGs...

For the rune circle I'm drawing a transparent 100x100 canvas with an orange stroked circle, inner triangle, and valknut shape scaled to render crisply at 256px. Then I'm building a rune band strip with a gray background and simple glyph lines spaced evenly across the width.

Now I'm working through the skeleton rig: mapping which joint in the spine chain the hips and pelvis mesh attach to, deciding the pelvis is an icosahedron sphere scaled to a hip shape, and figuring out which joint index the legs should branch from off the spine chain.

Still writing chain setup...

Working out hip and shoulder positions for hind and front legs with appropriate limb lengths and knee bend directions, then setting up the tail chain with spikes placed along a Catmull-Rom curve.

I'll also add a small dorsal ridge of spikes along each neck sweep, keeping them oriented outward from the curve. For the neck radii, I'm using a function that tapers thinner toward the ends but bulges slightly thicker in the center necks.

Mapping out the neck curve points per index, I'm varying head height and base/top x-offsets so the outer necks stay shorter and the center one reaches higher, with each S-curve bending back slightly before sweeping forward into the head -- and making sure the radius tapering keeps adjacent necks from clipping into each other.

Now I'm figuring out head orientation: tilting each head down about 25 degrees, using the neck's end direction as the forward axis with a perpendicular local frame, and rounding the neck-to-head joint with a cap sphere so the transition looks smooth. I also need eye decal placement computed relative to each head's direction vector, and a scaling factor for each head.

Writing the collar helix path...

Still placing decals...

I'm also getting the chest rune positioned by raycasting against the body surface to find where it sits on the torso, then adding a belly plate or emblem for extra detail.

Now I'm adding flank glyph decals on both sides as a magic seal motif, then moving on to building the spear: a wooden shaft with a splintered spike at the tip and a cloth strip trailing off it via a bezier curve.

Writing cloth sweep code...

I'm adding a small coordinate helper function, then checking ground contact points across feet, claws, and tail to make sure everything sits properly above the ground plane.

Still defining paint layers...

Finalizing the full code now...
